title: Base change compatibility of the direct-image counit
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] whose structure morphism is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X$ be a $k$-rational point [def-pc-rational-point]. Assume that for every scheme $T$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ the module category on $X_T$ has injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a morphism $i:T'\to T$ over $k$ and an object $\mathcal L\in F(T)$ of the invertible-direct-image subfunctor [def-pc-f-subfunctor] of the normalized Picard functor [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor], the pullback along the induced base-change map of the adjunction counit $f_T^*f_{T,*}\mathcal L\to\mathcal L$ is isomorphic as an arrow to the counit $f_{T'}^*f_{T',*}(i_X^*\mathcal L)\to i_X^*\mathcal L$ for the pulled-back object.

proof.text: By membership in $F(T)$ [def-pc-f-subfunctor], $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal L\cong\mathcal N[0]$ with $\mathcal N$ invertible [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]; taking $H^0$, $\mathcal N\cong f_{T,*}\mathcal L$. The module $\mathcal L$ is quasi-coherent and flat over $T$: it is invertible over $X_T$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and $X_T\to T$ is flat because $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The morphism $f_T:X_T\to T$ is quasi-compact and separated, being a base change of the projective, hence separated and quasi-compact, morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ (Stacks 01K5, 01K3). Apply the derived flat base-change theorem [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module] to the cartesian square defined by $i:T'\to T$ and $f_T$: $Li^*Rf_{T,*}\mathcal L\cong Rf_{T',*}i_X^*\mathcal L$. Since $\mathcal N$ is flat, $Li^*(\mathcal N[0])=(i^*\mathcal N)[0]$, so taking $H^0$ shows that the canonical base-change map $\beta:i^*f_{T,*}\mathcal L\to f_{T',*}i_X^*\mathcal L$ (the map adjoint to $f_{T'}^*i^*f_{T,*}\mathcal L\cong i_X^*f_T^*f_{T,*}\mathcal L\xrightarrow{i_X^*\varepsilon}i_X^*\mathcal L$, of which the derived comparison is the derived version, Stacks 02N6) is an isomorphism.

Write $c:i_X^*f_T^*\cong f_{T'}^*i^*$ for the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition], and $\varepsilon_T,\varepsilon_{T'}$ for the counits of the pullback/pushforward adjunctions [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Since $\beta$ of Step 1 is by definition the adjoint of $i_X^*\varepsilon_T\circ c^{-1}$, the triangle identity of the adjunction for $f_{T'}$ gives $\varepsilon_{T',i_X^*\mathcal L}\circ f_{T'}^*\beta\circ c=i_X^*\varepsilon_{T,\mathcal L}$. As $f_{T'}^*\beta\circ c$ is an isomorphism (Step 1), this commuting square, with the identity of $i_X^*\mathcal L$ (composed with the chosen isomorphism of $i_X^*\mathcal L$ with the representative of the pulled-back class) on the target edge, is an isomorphism in `Arrow` from the pullback of the counit for $\mathcal L$ to the counit for $i_X^*\mathcal L$, which is the asserted `Nonempty` witness.
